# nonPresentation

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a presentation.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonPresentation() — Checks whether a value is **not** a presentation. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/slide</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonPresentation<T>(value: T | GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Presentation): value is T;
```

`nonPresentation(value)` is the same test as `!isPresentation(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard looks for the methods that define the type — `getId`, `getSlides`. A stub that implements them passes, which is what makes code using this guard testable outside the runtime.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                        | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| GoogleAppsScript.Slides.Presentation` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a presentation; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const presentation = SlidesApp.getActivePresentation();

nonPresentation({}); // => true
nonPresentation(null); // => true
nonPresentation(presentation); // => false
```
